Discourse confirms it: 93:1-2 is a qasam and 93:3 is its jawāb, the classic frame for mā nāfiya over a māḍī (no lām al-qasam needed with negated jawāb). It is not mā al-ḥijāziyya (ʿāmila ʿamal laysa) because that requires a nominal clause; here the entry is verbal, so it is the non-operative negation particle, mabnī ʿalā al-sukūn, lā maḥall lahā min al-iʿrāb. The parallel وَمَا قَلَىٰ repeats the same particle under ʿaṭf.

votes.grammatical_reason: The token fuses two words in rasm: the preposition lām + اللَّه with ḥadhf of hamzat al-waṣl after the lām (hence the shadda-carrying لّ opening the token). The lām is a genuine ḥarf jarr, mabnī ʿalā al-kasr, and directly governs the lafẓ al-jalāla in jarr with a visible kasra. Semantically it is lām al-milk/al-ikhtiṣāṣ. Syntactically the sentence is a classic taqdīm al-khabar structure: the prepositional phrase stands first as khabar muqaddam (formally: muta'alliq to an elided khabar) and the mawṣūl مَا follows as mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar — fronting motivated by ḥaṣr (exclusivity of ownership). Both MCP sources state this explicitly (خبر مقدّم / شبه الجملة في محل رفع خبر مقدّم).

votes.grammatical_reason: إِنَّ (word 22) is the full operative form of the nāsikh (unlike the āyah-initial إِنَّمَا, where the kāffa مَا cancels its government). It enters a nominal clause and performs its canonical double operation: naṣb of the ism and rafʿ of the khabar. اللَّهَ immediately follows it as its ism, bearing the visible fatḥa of naṣb; غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ follow with visible ḍamma-tanwīn as its (double) khabar. No alternative parse competes: the noun cannot be a mafʿūl (no governing verb) nor a mubtadaʾ (it would then be marfūʿ). The contrast with إِنَّمَا at the āyah's head is the decisive canary point: مَا al-kāffa suppresses government there, while here the un-kaffed إِنَّ governs fully.
